E03.section: CLI best practices > Configure your workspace environment > Write a codebase rule file
E03.quote: Create a GEMINI.md or AGENTS.md file at your workspace root to outline specific directory standards, styling paradigms, test command parameters, and deprecation warnings. The agent automatically parses these rules on startup and consults them before suggesting changes.

E04.page_title: Choose an execution mode - Antigravity CLI | Google Antigravity Docs
E04.section_spec: Choose an execution mode > Analyze tasks before editing with plan mode
E04.section: Choose an execution mode > Analyze tasks before editing with plan mode
E04.quote: When plan mode is active through Shift+Tab cycling or the --mode flag, the CLI automatically prepends the /plan instruction prefix to your prompts. The agent investigates relevant files using read-only tools ( code_search , grep_search , view_file ) and presents a structured execution outline for your approval before writing code.
E04.claim_summary: Plan mode enables producing a structured execution outline for user approval before code changes.
E04.version_or_update: unversioned page; identified by access date and SHA-256

E05.quote: Artifact review policies : Configure whether the agent pauses for plan approval using your project’s artifact review policy . Proceed : Click Proceed to transition the agent into execution mode. The agent follows the approved plan step-by-step, validating each milestone with tests.

E45.page_title: Model quotas (/usage) - Antigravity CLI | Google Antigravity Docs
E45.quote: Antigravity CLI provides the /usage command (alias /quota) to help you monitor your resource consumption. When run, the command refreshes your model configuration and quota status from the backend and opens an interactive TUI panel.
E45.claim_summary: The CLI supports interactive usage monitoring with automatic refresh from backend.

E47.page_title: Headless mode - Antigravity CLI | Google Antigravity Docs
E47.section_spec: Headless mode > Permissions in headless mode
E47.section: Headless mode > Permissions in headless mode
E47.quote: By default, the CLI respects the permission mode in your settings. A tool that requires approval it can’t obtain is soft-denied: the run continues, exits 0 , and prints a notice to stderr naming the tool and how to allow it.
E47.claim_summary: In headless mode, permission approvals are handled by policy with soft-denies for unapproved tools.
